text: No existing game or wargame does what bavovniatko is aiming for; the prior art falls into five groups, each capturing a different piece of the Russo-Ukrainian war.
notes: Uncited synthesis in the overview; cited here to the review of commercial wargames that 08/0004 cites for the same point.

text: Modern RTS and tactical games such as Broken Arrow, WARNO, Regiments and Combat Mission: Black Sea model massed combined arms between NATO-style and Russian forces.
Broken Arrow's unit classes are infantry, recon, vehicles, support, helicopters and air; it has no drone class.
In Broken Arrow, drones are recon or strike aircraft that sit inside the air-defence matrix.
In 2026, loitering munitions were still only a roadmap item for Broken Arrow.
WARNO is set in 1989.
Regiments is set in 1989.
Combat Mission: Black Sea depicts a fictional 2017 Russia–Ukraine war and includes UAVs and EW.
Combat Mission: Black Sea was designed in 2009–2013 and deliberately avoids the "frozen conflict" that followed 2014.
Combat Mission: Black Sea has had no official 2022-era content since the Russian full-scale invasion.

Operational and strategic simulations of the real Russo-Ukrainian war exist mostly as community scenarios or small indie titles, such as a TOAW IV "Ukraine 2022" scenario and Sand Table's Ukraine War 2022.
Command: Modern Operations' Ukraine-2022 scenarios are mostly hypothetical NATO interventions.
The best commercial models of an operational layer are Cold War and WWII titles, such as Flashpoint Campaigns with WEGO orders and SOPs on 500 m hexes.
Steel Division 2 is a strong commercial model of an operational layer: a turn-based battalion campaign wrapped around real-time battles.
The one large-audience RTS of the 2022 war, Ukrainian Warfare: Gostomel Heroes, is told from the Russian side.
Drone games and trainers, many of them Ukrainian, are first-person and cover one drone at a time; examples are UFDS, Obriy, Remote Reaper and the arcade Death From Above.
Drone games and trainers model piloting, bombs and sometimes EW, but never the formation or operational picture.
Hell Of War, in early access from September 2026, is the first attempt to join the drone view and the command picture: it puts the player in a command drone that can drop into an FPV.
Board and professional wargames are the most thoughtful about logistics, politics and attrition, but they cluster at the start of the war or at grand-strategic scale.
GMT's Defiance covers February to April 2022.
Farren's Glory to the Heroes board wargame uses 150 km hexes.
Expert reviewers say that "relatively few of the existing commercial wargames" capture the dispersed, drone-saturated battlefield of 2025.

observations.subject: Russian tank
observations.note: the table does not say damaged or destroyed

text: As of January 2026, the Army of Drones Bonus planned points for air defence and aviation against drones and for snipers, and "depth coefficients" for strikes on logistics and UAV crews.
In March 2026 the Army of Drones Bonus still paid 12 points for a kill.
By March 2026, sniping, mobile fire groups and army aviation were scored in the Army of Drones Bonus, and points could buy components.
In March 2026, 12 points were proposed for a confirmed self-destruction of a Russian soldier.

observations.subject: confirmed self-destruction of a Russian soldier (proposed)

text: From March to May 2026, Delta scored reconnaissance detections of high-value targets more than 15 km behind the line and ranked units monthly.

observations.subject: minimum depth behind the line for Delta-scored reconnaissance detections

text: In June 2026, reconnaissance, logistics and evacuation missions earned Army of Drones Bonus points, and more than 800 products were listed on the Brave1 Market.

observations.subject: products listed on the Brave1 Market

text: Outlets keep repeating stale Army of Drones Bonus values: a June 2026 piece still quoted "roughly six points" per kill, so every value used should be dated.

text: Defiance: 2nd Russo-Ukrainian War 2022-? is a GMT Games board wargame designed by D. B. Dockter and Mark Herman.
Defiance covers the Kyiv and Chernihiv campaigns from 24 February to about 1 April 2022 in 3–4 day turns.
Defiance has five political tracks (Zelenskyy, NATO, Lukashenko, Putin, Russian MoD), supply, drones/air/missiles, VOVK partisans and a solitaire bot.
GMT's page for Defiance read "At the Printer".
notes: Status as read at access (research file accessed 2026-09-28).

text: The Defiance designer diary folds drones into detection and recon-strike and abstracts EW.
Defiance ties Russian supply to railheads within about 50 miles.

metric_new.label: Supply radius from a railhead or depot

observations.subject: Defiance Russian supply range from railheads

text: Defiance lets troop quality outweigh force ratios.
The Defiance designer diary calls the game "a first draft of history".
Ukrainian Crisis, by Brian Train, was a print-and-play game in March 2014 and was boxed by Hollandspiele in 2017.
Ukrainian Crisis is the precedent for designing a game while events unfold.
In Ukrainian Crisis, players spend finite chits across force, diplomacy, propaganda and prestige, and the conflict may never turn kinetic.
Glory to the Heroes is a free print-and-play grand-strategic wargame by Maj Ed Farren of the British Army, derived from Philip Sabin's designs.
Farren's Glory to the Heroes uses 150 km hexes and monthly turns and models attrition, climate, strategic bombing and propaganda.
Farren's Glory to the Heroes board wargame shares its name with Deaf Tone's shooter but is unrelated.
BoardGameGeek listings found by search include 2022: Ukraine (the first year of the war), Putin's War 2022, Ukraine 2022: Tabletop Wargame and To Kyiv!; only their existence is confirmed.
Farren's Glory to the Heroes circulates through PAXsims as a teaching tool.
A Marine Corps University wargame run two weeks before the Russian invasion anticipated the main axes of attack.
The Marine Corps University pre-invasion wargame erred by having Russia destroy Ukrainian air defences first, and it could not model Zelenskyy's leadership or Ukrainian morale.
The Marine Corps University long-war follow-up wargame used three-month turns and modelled drones, munitions depletion, mobilisation, aid and sanctions.

observations.subject: Marine Corps University long-war game turn

text: The Marine Corps University long-war wargame forecast stalemate and found that political objectives overrode military advice.
Earlier RAND Baltic wargaming shows how pre-2022 professional wargaming centred on NATO–Russia massed manoeuvre.
Eight US–Ukrainian tabletop exercises shaped the plan for the 2023 counteroffensive.

observations.subject: US–Ukrainian tabletop exercises before the 2023 counteroffensive

text: A senior Ukrainian officer said after the 2023 counteroffensive that the wargaming methods "doesn't work" given ubiquitous drones, trenches and no air superiority.
Brynen argues for proper post-mortems of the 2023 counteroffensive wargames rather than rejecting wargaming.
RUSI describes the 2025 battlefield as having three zones: a contested zone, a middle zone of about 30 km and a deep zone.
RUSI describes a seven-phase offensive cycle on the 2025 battlefield.
RUSI describes the 2025 battlefield as fought by small dispersed packets, with EW integral down to platoon level.
RUSI says FPV crews in 2025 "can see far more targets than they can hit".

cites.quote: can see far more targets than they can hit

text: In 2025, soft vehicles cannot operate within about 10 km of the front.

observations.subject: band where soft vehicles cannot operate

text: In 2025, resupply near the front goes by foot, quad bike, horse and UAV.
Few commercial wargames model the 2025 battlefield of dispersed packets, a no-vehicle band near the front and foot, quad, horse and UAV resupply.

Interviews with trainers in Germany found that the German colonel running staff training for Ukrainians "used a wargame scenario straight out of the Cold War, refusing to add drones and other modern weaponry".

cites.quote: used a wargame scenario straight out of the Cold War, refusing to add drones and other modern weaponry

text: The US training group for Ukrainian forces cited "broken simulation platforms" in 2025.
Ukrainian trainees rejected a Western drone course until it was rebuilt around frontline tactics in June 2025.
A retired US general argues for digital games as training for fights full of "electronic jamming, drones, sensors, and missiles".

text: Russia has codified PC-based simulator training for drone and anti-drone operators.
NATO–Russia wargames since 2025 put drones at the centre.
In a December 2025 game by Die Welt and the German Wargaming Center (Helmut Schmidt University), Russia seized Marijampolė with about 15,000 troops.

text: The ARRC's exercise Arrcade Strike in May 2026 rehearsed defending Estonia in 2030 from a "Ukraine-style bunker" under Charing Cross station.
The Arrcade Strike plan has thousands of drones lead the counterattack.
The British Army is estimated to be 80–90% short of the drones it needs and would run out in under a week at a few hundred drones a day.

observations.subject: British Army shortfall of needed drones
British Army drone consumption in the scenario

text: Canadian Army structure games in 2024–26, run by Maj Ed Farren, reached the lesson that "a platoon with a drone is better than platoon without a drone, but that wasn't the problem".

cites.quote: a platoon with a drone is better than platoon without a drone, but that wasn't the problem

text: The Canadian Army structure games found that the enemy's "sense and strike complex was pretty much unassailable" by jamming, counter-UAS or counter-battery fire.

cites.quote: sense and strike complex was pretty much unassailable

text: Since 2019, Dstl and Slitherine/Matrix Pro Simulations have built professional wargames on commercial game technology.
The Dstl–Slitherine wargames have been used for contingency planning, British Army structure and "the potential of remote and autonomous systems".

cites.quote: the potential of remote and autonomous systems

text: Dstl claims its wargames built on commercial game technology cut analysis time and cost by 50%.
No public Dstl game specifically on Ukraine's drone lessons was found.
From December 2022 to May 2023, volunteers used Steel Beasts PE to run brigade and battalion command post exercises for newly generated Ukrainian formations.
The volunteers training Ukrainian formations integrated JCATS, SBPro and VBS3, with VBS3 drones feeding the commanders' picture.
By 2025 the National Guard of Ukraine had adopted a Ukrainian-localised Steel Beasts Pro.
VBS4 ships Ukrainian terrain with drones and loitering munitions.
The VBS4 vendor concedes that brigade operations, logistics and morale were weak points of the simulation.
Domestic Ukrainian tools fill the drone and air-defence end of military simulation: UFDS and Obriy for crews and interceptors, and the MoD-codified Chaika VR trainers for shooting down drones.
Russian command-staff games (KShVI) rehearse procedure, including EW and counter-UAV, but do not test assumptions.
The Russian KShVI games' failure to test assumptions left Russian planners blind to drone saturation and ISR transparency.
A September 2026 GPT-assisted negotiation game was drafted in about two hours.

Usachova reads Play for Ukraine, in which players ran DDoS attacks on websites said to serve the Russian army, as a "resistance pleasure" that turns players into "digital soldiers".
In Play for Ukraine, the game is a weapon rather than a representation of war.
GSC Game World paused S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 at the Russian invasion and moved part of its team to Prague.
Volodymyr Yezhov, one of GSC Game World's original developers, was killed near Bakhmut in December 2022.
In November 2025 Russia declared GSC Game World "undesirable", citing about $17m it had sent to a fund that bought strike drones.

observations.subject: GSC Game World donations to a fund that bought strike drones

text: Frogwares' staff split between humanitarian work, the volunteer army and hybrid work during the invasion.
Frogwares pulled its games from sale in Russia.
4A Games had moved its headquarters from Kyiv to Malta in 2014.
Best Way's Men of War II was delayed by the Russian invasion.
Playing as Russians is a red line for many Ukrainians.
When Deaf Tone Games brought back Russian-faction PvP in Glory to the Heroes, Ukrainian press and players pushed back.
The Ukrainian backlash to Russian-faction play supports bavovniatko's Ukraine-only player stance.
Propaganda games are the mirror-image pitfall to Ukrainian-made war games.
Squad 22: ZOV was made with Russian Ministry of Defence backing.
Squad 22: ZOV frames the Russian invasion as "liberation" and is marketed for cadet and Yunarmy training.
Ukrainian Warfare: Gostomel Heroes (March 2026) is a more polished propaganda game that reaches a global audience, opening with "the brilliant Russian airborne assault" on Hostomel.
Ukrainian Warfare: Gostomel Heroes has about 2,000 mostly positive Steam reviews.
The developer of Ukrainian Warfare: Gostomel Heroes calls its next project another game "on the topic of the Special Military Operation".

cites.quote: on the topic of the Special Military Operation

text: The free DLC for Ukrainian Warfare: Gostomel Heroes adds a skirmish map of Bucha.
The store title of Gostomel Heroes reads as Ukrainian, which shows how naming alone can launder a perspective.
Roblox war games let children play either side of the Russo-Ukrainian war.
Arma 3 footage keeps being passed off as real combat footage from Ukraine.
The CEO of UFDS calls selling a combat trainer as a game "a very sensitive question".
War on the Rocks warns that Army of Drones Bonus-style points invite Goodhart's-law distortions.
War on the Rocks warns that Army of Drones Bonus-style points blur civilian reporting into targeting.
The March 2026 proposal to pay e-points when a cornered Russian soldier kills himself shows how a points schema is pulled into ever darker edge cases.
A critic quoted on the Death From Above store page calls its mix of politics and games uncomfortable.

text: Dockter and Herman say that "wiser men and women would avoid" designing a game of an ongoing war, and that it is still worth doing as a first draft of history.

cites.quote: wiser men and women would avoid

text: Real-time strategy games such as Broken Arrow mass armour and air.
Drone games such as UFDS put the player in a single drone.
No existing game gives the company-to-brigade commander dispersed 2–3 person positions, drone crews, EW and a ~10 km no-vehicle belt.
The kill-zone commander is an empty niche in games, and bavovniatko should aim for it.
Hell Of War, the nearest attempt at a kill-zone commander game, makes a command drone the main camera but is still a hero game with a fire-support budget.
The Canadian Army games' lesson belongs at bavovniatko's core: the problem to solve is the enemy's sense-and-strike complex, not one's own number of drones.
Radio-only fog-of-war games were faulted for reports that are too precise.
The fog of the Russo-Ukrainian war is the opposite of radio-only games' fog: commanders see more targets than they can hit.
bavovniatko should model detection as abundant and effectors, sorties and battery or fibre as scarce.
Ukraine's own Army of Drones Bonus scoring now pays for deep detections (more than 15 km behind the line) separately from strikes, a ready-made split between sensing and killing.

observations.subject: minimum depth behind the line for Delta-scored reconnaissance detections

text: Most games abstract supply into radii, as the TOAW IV Ukraine 2022 scenario does.
bavovniatko should make last-mile resupply by foot, quad, horse and UAV a core, player-managed and interdictable system.

bavovniatko should model EW as signal physics rather than a buff, using the Arma Reforger drone mod's line-of-sight, occlusion, jamming and RSSI/LQ model as a template and tying it to era-gated countermeasures so the measure/countermeasure cycle is systemic.
bavovniatko's EW model should add Remote Reaper's split between control and video links and its terrain loss between ground station and drone.
bavovniatko should avoid Broken Arrow's shortcut of treating drones as small helicopters for air defence to shoot at.
The TOAW IV engine forced its Ukraine 2022 scenario to fake Javelins.
Obriy updates its terrain as the front moves.
Defiance stops at April 2022.
No competitor covers eras e8 and e9 at operational scale, so bavovniatko should keep equipment and doctrine as per-era data (e1…e9).
A points-for-effects requisition economy is authentic for bavovniatko, since the real Army of Drones Bonus gets repriced like a live game.
bavovniatko's requisition economy should weight capture, evacuation and depth strikes the way the real Army of Drones Bonus schema does.
In bavovniatko's requisition economy, Goodhart-style distortions should surface as a mechanic, not a high score.

Political objectives overriding military advice, Defiance's political tracks and Train's non-kinetic chits all point to a political layer in bavovniatko that issues orders from above ("hold this town") that the player cannot refuse.
bavovniatko should make the player Ukrainian only.
bavovniatko should keep a stylised, non-photoreal drone feed with a visible game HUD so that clips cannot pass as real footage.
bavovniatko should have a civilian presence without gamifying civilian harm.
bavovniatko should show no kill-count leaderboards.

Because Russian staff games rehearse procedure rather than adapt, a scripted, wave-based assault AI for the Russian opponent that adapts slowly across eras is supported for bavovniatko.
